To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RNA can alter the mode of recognition of a promoter by the RdRp, and that the RNA can direct the mode of promoter utilization by the RdRp.

the brome mosaic viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) recognizes the BMV core promoter in the same way that it recognizes the CCMV core promoter and that the BMV RdRp can be induced to recognize the CCMV promoter in the same mode as it recognizes the BMV promoter.

the brome mosaic and cowpea mosaic viruses have similar subgenomic RNA promoters but that the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) of cowpea mosaic virus recognizes the subgenomic RNA promoter in an altered manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that govern subgenomic RNA replication in bromoviruses and with the molecular mechanisms of RNA-RNA recognition.
the mechanism of recognition by viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRP) of the RNA template.
the mechanisms of RNA synthesis in plant RNA viruses, particularly those that utilize a subgenomic RNA promoter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BMV and CCMV RdRp's recognize the subgenomic promoter of the other virus in the same manner as their own subgenomic promoter.
both RdRps recognize the same nucleotide sequence at the subgenomic promoter, but the mode of recognition is different.

the BMV RdRp recognizes the BMV promoter with an absolute requirement for nucleotides at -17, -13, -14, and -11 and a preference for nucleotides A at -12, -10, -8, -6, -4, and +2, whereas the CCMV RdRp requires nucleotides at the -20, -17, -15, -14, 13, -12, -11, -10, and -8 positions
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRP) of the bromovirus brome mosaic virus is a highly specific enzyme.
the subgenomic promoters of BMV and CCMV are recognized differently by the same viral RdRps, and the mode of recognition is determined by the sequence of the promoter.
both the BMV and CCMV RdRps recognize the subgenomic promoter with the same mode of binding, however, the CCMV RdRp requires an additional four nucleotides to recognize the promoter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RNA can dictate the mode of promoter binding and recognition by the RdRp.
the RNA can direct the RdRp to change how it recognizes a promoter.
the RNA can direct the mode of recognition of viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRP).
